plan: [ This is a sealed-bid second-price auction with independent private values. For risk-neutral bidders, bidding truthfully (bid = value) is a weakly dominant strategy: it maximizes expected profit regardless of others’ strategies, since you only pay the second-highest bid if you win. There is no useful history (only 1 round). Avoid overbidding (risk negative surplus if second-highest exceeds value) and underbidding (risk losing profitable wins). I will bid my exact value: $33.0. ]

[ Second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values: the dominant, profit-maximizing strategy is to bid your true value. No history to exploit and values are redrawn, so no strategic shading. With value $10 and $0.1 increments, bidding exactly 10 captures surplus when the second-highest bid is below 10 and avoids overpaying. Bid 10.0. ]

[ This is a sealed-bid second-price (Vickrey) auction with independent private values. The weakly dominant strategy is to bid my true value: if I win, I pay the second-highest bid, so bidding higher doesn’t change the price paid and risks overpaying only in non-Vickrey formats; bidding lower risks losing when winning would be profitable. With no prior-round info and one round only, I’ll bid exactly my value, $21. Ties, if any, are random; bidding truthfully still maximizes expected profit. ]
